headline: Warm, dry Friday, then light rain Saturday and cooler, mostly dry weather.
summary: High pressure keeps western Washington dry and warm through Friday, with inland highs in the mid to upper 70s. Fog should stay limited Friday morning, with a few patches possible in the south Sound. Breezy east winds tonight will gust to 25 to 30 mph in the Cascades and foothills. Saturday, a weak front brings light rain, a few hundredths of an inch for most lowlands and about a quarter inch in the mountains, with central Puget Sound possibly getting less. Sunday is cool and mostly dry. A low-pressure system is likely to pass south of the area Monday, keeping it dry and cool, though not all computer models agree. Another weak front may bring isolated showers Wednesday into Thursday.
changes: The morning discussion expected heavier Saturday rain, with the coast and north most likely to get it, plus possible afternoon showers and a convergence zone over Snohomish County. Later discussions dropped those details, describing only light rain and leaning toward a dry Monday.
